chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Allah is merciful to the servant due to the intensity of his love for his child.
ai.seo_question: How does a parent's love for their child relate to Allah's mercy?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni uses this narration to ground the ethical duty of kindness to children in divine mercy, suggesting that parental affection serves as a spiritual conduit for Allah's compassion. This aligns with the Shia emphasis on *birr* (righteousness) within the family unit, where natural human emotions are sanctified when directed towards one's offspring. The hadith implies that the intensity of love is not merely emotional but carries theological weight in the balance of deeds.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from the one who mentioned it, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> is merciful to the servant due to the intensity of his love for his child’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from those whom he has mentioned who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Allah will have mercy on (His) slave because of his intense love for his children.’”
